knowledge_point.title: Evaluating Surface Integrals Over Parametric Surfaces

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the surface integral

$$
\iint_S f(x,y,z)\,\mathrm{d}S,
$$

where $f(x,y,z)=4 x y$ and

$$
\mathbf r(u,v)=\langle v, u, - 2 u - 3 v + 6\rangle
$$

for $0\le u\le 3$ and $0\le v\le 3$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a scalar surface integral, use

$$
\iint_S f\,\mathrm{d}S=\iint_D f(\mathbf r(u,v))\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\|\,\mathrm{d}A.
$$

Differentiate the coordinate functions:

$$
\mathbf r_u=\langle 0, 1, -2\rangle,\qquad\mathbf r_v=\langle 1, 0, -3\rangle.
$$

The cross product and positive area factor are

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v&=\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf i&\mathbf j&\mathbf k\\0&1&-2\\1&0&-3\end{vmatrix} \\
&=\langle -3, -2, -1\rangle, \\
\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\|&=\sqrt{(-3)^2+(-2)^2+(-1)^2}=\sqrt{14}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Substitute the coordinates and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}
f(\mathbf r(u,v))&=4 \left(v\right) \left(u\right) \\
&=4 u v.
\end{aligned}
$$

Integrate over the parameter rectangle:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\iint_S f\,\mathrm{d}S&=\sqrt{14}\int_{0}^{3}\int_{0}^{3}\left(4 u v\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\,\mathrm{d}v \\
&=\sqrt{14}\int_{0}^{3}\left[2 u^{2} v\right]_{u=0}^{u=3}\,\mathrm{d}v \\
&=\sqrt{14}\int_{0}^{3}\left(18 v\right)\,\mathrm{d}v \\
&=\sqrt{14}\left[9 v^{2}\right]_{v=0}^{v=3} \\
&=\sqrt{14}\left(\left(81\right)-\left(0\right)\right) \\
&=81 \sqrt{14}.
\end{aligned}
$$

knowledge_point.title: Evaluating Surface Integrals Over Parametric Surfaces

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the surface integral

$$
\iint_S f(x,y,z)\,\mathrm{d}S,
$$

where $f(x,y,z)=x^{2} - z^{2}$ and

$$
\mathbf r(u,v)=\langle 2 u + v, 2 u - 2 v, u + 2 v\rangle
$$

for $-2\le u\le -1$ and $2\le v\le 3$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a scalar surface integral, use

$$
\iint_S f\,\mathrm{d}S=\iint_D f(\mathbf r(u,v))\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\|\,\mathrm{d}A.
$$

Differentiate the coordinate functions:

$$
\mathbf r_u=\langle 2, 2, 1\rangle,\qquad\mathbf r_v=\langle 1, -2, 2\rangle.
$$

The cross product and positive area factor are

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v&=\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf i&\mathbf j&\mathbf k\\2&2&1\\1&-2&2\end{vmatrix} \\
&=\langle 6, -3, -6\rangle, \\
\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\|&=\sqrt{(6)^2+(-3)^2+(-6)^2}=9.
\end{aligned}
$$

Substitute the coordinates and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}
f(\mathbf r(u,v))&=\left(2 u + v\right)^{2} - \left(u + 2 v\right)^{2} \\
&=3 u^{2} - 3 v^{2}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Integrate over the parameter rectangle:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\iint_S f\,\mathrm{d}S&=9\int_{2}^{3}\int_{-2}^{-1}\left(3 u^{2} - 3 v^{2}\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\,\mathrm{d}v \\
&=9\int_{2}^{3}\left[u^{3} - 3 u v^{2}\right]_{u=-2}^{u=-1}\,\mathrm{d}v \\
&=9\int_{2}^{3}\left(7 - 3 v^{2}\right)\,\mathrm{d}v \\
&=9\left[- v^{3} + 7 v\right]_{v=2}^{v=3} \\
&=9\left(\left(-6\right)-\left(6\right)\right) \\
&=-108.
\end{aligned}
$$

knowledge_point.title: Evaluating Surface Integrals Over Parametric Surfaces

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the surface integral

$$
\iint_S f(x,y,z)\,\mathrm{d}S,
$$

where $f(x,y,z)=x^{2} - 2 y z$ and

$$
\mathbf r(u,v)=\langle u + v, u, v\rangle
$$

for $-2\le u\le -1$ and $-1\le v\le 1$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a scalar surface integral, use

$$
\iint_S f\,\mathrm{d}S=\iint_D f(\mathbf r(u,v))\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\|\,\mathrm{d}A.
$$

Differentiate the coordinate functions:

$$
\mathbf r_u=\langle 1, 1, 0\rangle,\qquad\mathbf r_v=\langle 1, 0, 1\rangle.
$$

The cross product and positive area factor are

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v&=\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf i&\mathbf j&\mathbf k\\1&1&0\\1&0&1\end{vmatrix} \\
&=\langle 1, -1, -1\rangle, \\
\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\|&=\sqrt{(1)^2+(-1)^2+(-1)^2}=\sqrt{3}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Substitute the coordinates and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}
f(\mathbf r(u,v))&=\left(u + v\right)^{2} - 2 \left(u\right) \left(v\right) \\
&=u^{2} + v^{2}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Integrate over the parameter rectangle:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\iint_S f\,\mathrm{d}S&=\sqrt{3}\int_{-1}^{1}\int_{-2}^{-1}\left(u^{2} + v^{2}\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\,\mathrm{d}v \\
&=\sqrt{3}\int_{-1}^{1}\left[\frac{u^{3}}{3} + u v^{2}\right]_{u=-2}^{u=-1}\,\mathrm{d}v \\
&=\sqrt{3}\int_{-1}^{1}\left(v^{2} + \frac{7}{3}\right)\,\mathrm{d}v \\
&=\sqrt{3}\left[\frac{v^{3}}{3} + \frac{7 v}{3}\right]_{v=-1}^{v=1} \\
&=\sqrt{3}\left(\left(\frac{8}{3}\right)-\left(- \frac{8}{3}\right)\right) \\
&=\frac{16 \sqrt{3}}{3}.
\end{aligned}
$$
